Is this object an orchestra manifest?

Source: R/manifest_class.R
is_orchestra_manifest.Rd

Tests contract identity tolerantly, accepting both the package-qualified class this package defines and the bare class minted by emitters that implement the contract without depending on this package.

Usage

is_orchestra_manifest(x)

Arguments

x

Any object.

Value

A length-1 logical, TRUE when x is an S7 object whose class vector contains an orchestra_manifest entry in either the bare or the package-qualified form.

Details

A strict S7::S7_inherits() check against the class object defined here would reject every manifest built anywhere else, including all of those already in circulation, because S7 records the defining package in the class identity. Since the contract is deliberately implementable without a dependency on this package, identity has to be tested on the class name, which is the part the contract actually fixes. The object must still be an S7 object, so an ordinary list carrying a lookalike class attribute does not pass.

See also

orchestra_manifest for the class, and its Class identity across homes section for why the tolerance is needed.

Author

Max Moldovan

Examples

m <- orchestra_manifest(
  emitter_package = "example",
  emitter_version = "0.1.0",
  inferential_target = "parameters",
  run_id = "example-001",
  method = "example:demo",
  timestamp = Sys.time(),
  data_hash = "sha256:example"
)
is_orchestra_manifest(m)
#> [1] TRUE
is_orchestra_manifest(list(a = 1))
#> [1] FALSE
